reasons: F01, F02, F03, F05, F06, F07: no material weakness, unqualified ICFR opinion, no auditor change or disagreements, and no prior-period corrections, so the control environment looks clean.

F09, F10, F08, F11, F24: no significant unbilled or contract assets, no bill-and-hold or channel return rights, revenue mostly recognised at a point in time, no material related-party transactions and no critical audit matter topics, which leaves little room for judgement-driven revenue manipulation.
R09, R17: Beneish M-score of -2.52 is well below the -1.78 threshold, and the Dechow F-score of 0.28 is well below 1.0.
R08, R10, R19: total and RSST accruals are slightly negative (-0.02), and operating cash flow is 1.23x net income, so earnings are backed by cash.

R01, R11, R18, R12: receivables growth runs slightly ahead of sales (DSRI 1.05, AR growth minus sales growth 0.05) and inventory rose modestly (0.02 of assets). These are minor and worth monitoring but are not red flags on their own.

R02, R04, R15, R14: gross margin improved (GMI 0.93) and ROA rose (+0.05) while sales were flat (SGI 1.0) and cash sales fell slightly. Higher profitability on flat revenue deserves a modest check of cost capitalisation and inventory costing.

F18: an undisclosed-type government investigation is ongoing. This is a contingent-liability and possibly compliance risk, not direct evidence of misstatement, and F16 confirms there is no SEC inquiry.
F26, R13: emphasis on non-GAAP measures and a fairly high soft-asset share (0.53) give some room for presentation and estimate-based judgement.

F14, F15, F19, F20, F21, F22, F23: no management turnover, no covenant pressure, no revenue or EPS-linked incentive pay, no capital raise, no acquisition and no SPAC history, so incentive and pressure indicators are low.
